title: Microsoft Bob, 1995
lede: A Windows shell that showed programs as objects in the rooms of a house, the extreme early case of the metaphor.
summary: A house with rooms; a pen and paper opens the word processor. Microsoft, 1995.

evidence.note: The only image found is a 288 × 216 px non-free screenshot on Wikipedia, too small to describe. Based on Wikipedia.

styles.note: A precursor: the whole computer becomes a set of household objects. It uses the metaphor fully but predates the material textures and bevels of 2007–2013.

context: Released on 10 March 1995 and discontinued in early 1996. “Microsoft Bob presented screens showing a house, with rooms that the user could visit containing familiar objects corresponding to computer applications, such as a desk with pen and paper and a checkbook. Clicking on the pen and paper would open the system’s word processor.” [Wikipedia: Microsoft Bob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Bob).

Wikipedia’s skeuomorph article names Bob as the extreme case of the desktop metaphor, “representing different programs as objects in a home.” [Wikipedia: Skeuomorph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeuomorph).
interpretation: Bob shows the metaphor without the later material realism. Its failure is a common warning against a metaphor that makes actions harder.
